sampling_model.design: The unrestricted benchmark ranges over every law on \(\mathcal A^n\) chosen independently of the complete schedule; the attaining design is iid \(q^\star\), and the allocation frontier ranges over iid triangular arrays \(q_n\).
sampling_model.units: There are \(n\) labelled units with a fixed complete binary schedule \(z\in\{0,1\}^{3n}\); no superpopulation sampling is invoked.
sampling_model.treatment: Each unit receives exactly one of three labelled arms and reveals \(Y_i(A_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity restriction is imposed on unrestricted competing designs; each iid frontier array is eventually in the interior because it converges to \(q^\star\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no estimated nuisance regressions. The nonlinear correction uses only the known allocation and the observed centered contrast score; all probability is assignment probability conditional on \(z\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For two-arm binary finite-population effects, unrestricted minimax risk is \(n^{-1}-(-4^{1/3}a_1')n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and balanced Bernoulli assignment with nonlinear shrinkage attains it.
For two bounded-outcome arms, iid half assignment and a nonlinear endpoint-derived estimator attain the unrestricted minimax value characterized by a finite convex program.
Under the paper's permutation-invariant uncertainty class and linear-estimation formulation, complete randomization and a Neyman allocation solve the stated minimax problem.
For general multi-treatment finite-population contrasts and assignment mechanisms, the paper gives exact variance identities for linear unbiased estimators.
For multi-arm complete randomization with fixed limiting allocation proportions, regression-adjusted estimators admit regular design-based asymptotic comparisons.
Second-order asymptotic minimax behavior can be characterized by square completion and a problem-specific differential operator.
Restricted normal-mean minimax risk has a boundary-layer analysis based on least-favorable distributions.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population total estimation, pairwise-independent sampling and midpoint-differenced Horvitz--Thompson estimation attain the sharp minimax criterion.

body.tldr: For the binary three-arm contrast \((1,-1/2,-1/2)\), start from the lossless exact labelled eight-type orbit game imported from the accepted repository parent. The new field-level kernel identifies the half-wedge Airy constant \(C_3=-a_1'\), transfers it uniformly through the singular \(\eta=0\) fiber while retaining null observation cells and dormant primal constraints, and derives the sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) iid allocation frontier with penalty \(2\zeta_1^2+4\zeta_2^2+4\zeta_3^2\). The resulting unrestricted and iid \(q^\star=(1/2,1/4,1/4)\) risks share the expansion \(n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\), supported by an Airy-feedback rule and a label-preserving, allocation-regularized complete-schedule prior.

project_justification.gap: The accepted repository parent settles the lossless exact multi-arm orbit reduction, but it does not identify the second-order constant, control the singular transverse fiber, or characterize allocation perturbations at the scale where first-order design loss meets nonlinear minimax gain.
project_justification.niche: For the symmetric active-arm-versus-pooled-comparators contrast, the inherited orbit game has an explicitly solvable half-wedge tangent geometry but a nonregular \(\eta=0\) bridge that is absent from scalar two-arm theory.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact half-wedge Airy constant, proves a uniform finite-orbit bridge with null-cell and dormant-constraint control, constructs matching upper and lower procedures, and establishes the necessary-and-sufficient \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation frontier.

body.related_work: The accepted repository parent \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\) supplies the lossless labelled eight-type orbit-game reduction used here as infrastructure. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorems 2.2 and 3.1 and Appendix C) inform the one-dimensional score correction, Airy prior, and lattice comparison, but do not resolve the half-wedge constant or the singular transverse bridge. Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and proof A.4) informs the endpoint-game and posterior-mean construction for two arms. Mukerjee, Dasgupta, and Rubin (2018, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) supply the arm-labelled setup for general treatment contrasts and unequal replication, with linear unbiased estimation and variance as their target. Bai (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3) informs the first-order allocation square completion; the new frontier couples its constrained Hessian to the nonregular \(n^{-4/3}\) experiment uniformly over \(n^{-1/6}\) perturbations. Zhao and Ding (2023) and Li and Ding (2017) provide regular multi-arm finite-population asymptotics, not uniform boundary-layer minimax expansions. Levit (1981) and Bickel (1981) inform the spectral and least-favorable-prior route. Aronow and Lopatto (2026, Theorems 1--3) study endpoint minimaxity under design unbiasedness, a restriction not imposed here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The value calculation alone is not the finite-experiment theorem. The lower bound fails if the posterior target is scalarized: under the half-effect prior its coefficient is \(b_{A_i}(\alpha)\), and the residual-variance term is needed to obtain \(I(f)+\{2\bar q_1-1/2\}m_1(f)\). The unrestricted prior also needs the vanishing broad component; the pure Airy component has a linear allocation sensitivity. Finally, \(\eta=0\) is a minimizing singular fiber, not a boundary of \(\mathbb R^2\); inserting an \(\eta\)-Laplacian or a transverse boundary condition would define the wrong experiment.
body.honest_scope: The lossless exact labelled eight-type orbit reduction is imported from the accepted repository parent and is not a contribution of this proposal. The half-wedge tangent program, exact Airy constant, posterior coefficient, uniform Airy upper remainder, allocation-coercive mixture lower bound, sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) frontier, and singular recovery comparison remain statements to prove. The first kill tests are to reproduce the labelled \(n=3\) gap, verify the posterior coefficient including conditional residual variance, and check allocation square completion uniformly over the closed simplex. The proposal does not claim uniqueness of the unrestricted design, equality with fixed-count complete randomization, full Le Cam equivalence of all nuisance experiments, or an endpoint extension beyond binary outcomes. On schedules satisfying \(Y_i(2)=Y_i(3)\), the construction must reduce to the published balanced two-arm shifted-binomial experiment.
